##### Validation and interpretation limits

Actual batch hashes and every learning-rate value match the reference at every checkpoint. All gradients are finite and post-clip norms respect the threshold within float32 tolerance. All 39 repository tests passed, including identity shortcut gradients, architecture shapes, common initialization, and inference checkpoint reconstruction.

The legacy norm2 health field means the final residual branch BatchNorm for residual_3, but the second convolution BatchNorm for the other architectures. These have different roles, so their gamma values should not be treated as directly equivalent feature scales.

One seed, a heavily repeated training subset (about 41 passes), and 64 held-out games limit conclusions. The residual comparison changes depth and shortcut structure together; it does not isolate shortcuts from depth. No playing-strength evaluation is included.

##### Best residual checkpoint full legal probe

The best saved residual checkpoint (40,000 updates) has legal NLL 3.2629 and legal top-1 accuracy 22.53% on all 6,147 validation moves.

##### Assessment

The deeper residual architecture is the strongest accuracy candidate. It improved raw and legal move accuracy,
with only 3.5% more parameters, and its best saved validation loss was at 40,000 updates. Its final legal NLL
was worse than the reference despite higher accuracy; the 40,000-update checkpoint had better legal NLL
(3.2629) than the final residual checkpoint (3.3423).

It did not eliminate long-run drift. In updates 40,001–80,000, clipping rose to 12.84%, versus 0.06% in the
reference, and BatchNorm parameter gradient tails grew. Global gradient p95 was 6.02, maximum 14.94;
all gradients were finite. This is substantially milder than sustained 100% clipping, but it is not evidence
that the full-scale instability has been solved. Raw validation loss rose while training loss fell.

The reduced head is a parameter-saving tradeoff: 14.6% fewer parameters, slightly better raw NLL,
better legal NLL, stable gradients, but lower raw and legal top-1 accuracy. It does not justify replacing
the existing head solely to improve move accuracy.

Dense activation concentration remained similar across cases (top four features carry about 12–13% of
activity). However, the final residual trunk was more concentrated: four of sixteen channels carried 65.7%
of activity, versus 37.5% in the reference and 33.7% in the reduced-head model. No trunk channel was dormant
on the sampled observations. Residual dense dormant fraction was 7.8%, versus 3.1% and 0% respectively.
Thus increased accuracy should not be described as uniformly healthier internal statistics.

For the next architecture, favor the residual trunk with the existing dense head and dropout 0.1, using
validation-based checkpoint selection. The smaller-data run supports the architecture's accuracy benefit;
it does not determine the best LR schedule or stopping epoch for the full dataset.

##### Cross-round empirical evidence

All rows below use the same 16-channel / 64-hidden architecture dimensions, cached data split, seed, 80k update budget, optimizer settings, and long LR horizon, except for the named intervention. The architecture changes use dropout 0.1. The reference baseline without dropout is the first row.

| Intervention | Best saved raw val NLL | Final raw val NLL | Final raw accuracy | Final-interval clipping |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Plain CNN, no dropout | 3.7138 | 3.7915 | 20.69% | 0.00% |
| No decay on norms/biases | 3.7140 | 3.7809 | 20.64% | 0.00% |
| Fixed BN affine | 3.8039 | 4.0995 | 18.92% | 42.84% |
| Dense BN, no dropout | 3.6913 | 3.8004 | 20.27% | 0.00% |
| Dropout 0.1 | 3.6342 | 3.6342 | 20.74% | 0.06% |
| Dropout 0.2 | 3.6515 | 3.6515 | 20.12% | 5.68% |
| Dense BN + dropout 0.1 | 3.6436 | 3.6690 | 20.42% | 0.00% |
| Three residual blocks + dropout 0.1 | 3.5724 | 3.6239 | 22.22% | 12.84% |
| Reduced head + dropout 0.1 | 3.6076 | 3.6076 | 20.01% | 0.08% |

These controls matter for causal claims: excluding norm/bias decay was nearly neutral in the plain model, and fixing BN affine parameters worsened validation loss and clipping. Dense BN improved feature balance without consistently improving predictions. Dropout 0.1 helped generalization and dense concentration, but neither dropout nor depth uniformly improved every internal statistic. Do not claim that weight decay on BN affine parameters has been established as the root cause.

##### Late-training diagnosis: observations versus hypotheses

**Observed schedule and data exposure.** The 80k stress test deliberately uses the first 80k steps of a 334,440-step schedule. LR at 20k, 40k, and 80k is approximately 9.95e-4, 9.74e-4, and 8.81e-4: 99.5%, 97.4%, and 88.1% of the 1e-3 peak. Training sees approximately 10.3, 20.6, and 41.2 dataset passes at these checkpoints. It never enters the low-LR finishing phase. This was an intentional matched stress-test design, not a scheduler implementation bug. It is a plausible contributor, not proof of causation. The original full cluster run completed its full decay and still clipped persistently; matching the pilot schedule to its endpoint alone cannot be claimed to solve that run.

**New post-hoc checks.** These evaluate existing checkpoints only; no additional training or temperature fitting was performed. Legal metrics cover all 6,147 held-out moves; ECE uses 15 equal-width confidence bins and should be interpreted with the limited 64-game validation set.

| Residual checkpoint | Legal accuracy | Mean top confidence | Legal NLL | Legal ECE | Legal Brier score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 20,000 | 22.30% | 34.40% | 3.2078 | 0.1210 | 0.9000 |
| 40,000 | 22.53% | 35.14% | 3.2629 | 0.1261 | 0.9015 |
| 80,000 | 23.07% | 37.10% | 3.3423 | 0.1403 | 0.9041 |

Accuracy rises, but confidence rises faster; legal NLL, ECE, and Brier score worsen. This supports probability overfitting / growing overconfidence rather than a total loss of predictive ability. Among evaluated checkpoints, **20k is best by legal NLL, 40k by raw NLL, and 80k by top-1 accuracy**. The training script currently selects best_policy.pt by raw NLL. For the deployed masked policy, also track/select on full validation legal NLL; do not silently equate these objectives.

**BN running-stat check.** Dropout was disabled in both modes. At 80k, raw NLL was 3.6239 using running statistics and 3.6839 using per-batch statistics; at 40k it was 3.5724 versus 3.5887. Batch-stat evaluation used the same ordered validation batches of 128 (last batch smaller), with running-buffer updates disabled. Fresh batch statistics did not rescue loss. This weakens the stale-running-stat explanation, but is not a proof that batch-stat noise never matters. Our dropout also follows all BN layers, so the standard dropout-before-BN variance-shift mechanism is not an obvious match to this architecture.

**Gradient scale versus optimizer step.** Late norm-parameter gradient tails increased, while sampled median actual relative updates decreased for the stem (0.130% to 0.097%), dense layer (0.154% to 0.094%), and policy head (0.0099% to 0.0056%) between the 20k–40k and 40k–80k intervals. The final residual branch BN relative update increased from 0.050% to 0.070%. All remain finite. Raw gradient growth is therefore not synonymous with runaway updates across the entire model. The last branch BN gamma falls from 0.258 at 40k to 0.137 at 80k; in a residual branch that does not mean the whole feature path has vanished because the shortcut remains.

**Working explanation.** Depth and shortcuts improve representation and gradient paths; they do not remove cross-entropy confidence growth, extensive dataset reuse, high late LR, or learnable normalization scales. The data support both probability overfitting and normalization-related gradient-scale drift. Their causal relationship has not been isolated.

##### Literature and how directly it applies

- [Guo et al., On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks, ICML 2017](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a/guo17a.pdf) document that NLL can overfit while classification accuracy continues improving. This is a close empirical match to our checkpoint trend; it supports separating confidence quality from accuracy.
- [van Laarhoven, L2 Regularization versus Batch and Weight Normalization, 2017](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05350) analyzes how normalization and regularization affect weight scales and effective learning rates, including limits of Adam scale compensation. Its scale-invariance results are not a proof that our learned BN gamma is the culprit.
- [Lobacheva et al., On the Periodic Behavior of Neural Network Training with Batch Normalization and Weight Decay, NeurIPS 2021](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/hash/b433da1b32b5ca96c0ba7fcb9edba97d-Abstract.html) show late destabilization from normalization/decay dynamics, with SGD-focused analysis and experiments. It establishes a possible mechanism, not a diagnosis of our AdamW run; our training loss still decreases and we have not demonstrated periodic cycles or the paper's full mechanism.
- [He et al., Bag of Tricks for Image Classification with Convolutional Neural Networks, CVPR 2019](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2019/papers/He_Bag_of_Tricks_for_Image_Classification_with_Convolutional_Neural_Networks_CVPR_2019_paper.pdf) empirically evaluate cosine LR decay, residual-branch zero-gamma initialization, and other refinements. This supports testing the training recipe rather than assuming another architecture change will fix the dynamics. Their exact hyperparameters are not established optima for our task.
- [Müller et al., When Does Label Smoothing Help?, NeurIPS 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.02629) find improved calibration and generalization in studied settings. Small legal-action-aware smoothing is a candidate for our overconfidence issue; naive uniform smoothing over all 4,096 classes would also assign target mass to illegal moves, so it is not a suitable drop-in prescription.
- [Li et al., Understanding the Disharmony Between Dropout and Batch Normalization by Variance Shift, CVPR 2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.05134) explain a train/eval variance mismatch when dropout feeds BN. Our dropout placement makes that specific explanation less applicable.
- [Wu and He, Group Normalization, ECCV 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08494) provide a normalization independent of batch composition. It is an alternative to test, but retains learned affine parameters and does not remove every normalization/weight-decay scale interaction.

##### Prioritized actions

1. **Earlier LR decay has now been tested in the follow-up below.** It reduced clipping but did not improve final NLL or calibration. The following was the original proposed ablation: keep architecture, AdamW, clipping at 5, and dropout 0.1 fixed. A clean pilot ablation keeps the same 5,820 warmup steps but completes cosine decay to 1e-5 within the actual 80k budget, rather than 334,440. Another option is a validation-triggered LR reduction. The precise schedule is our proposed experiment, not a literature-proven optimum. For the full dataset, choose decay timing in relation to actual data exposure and validation behavior; do not copy the pilot's 20k/40k stopping points blindly.
2. **Select checkpoints using the deployed policy's validation objective.** Retain raw and legal NLL plus accuracy. Our raw-NLL best checkpoint differs from the legal-NLL best checkpoint. Checkpoint selection protects against later degradation; it does not fix optimization dynamics.
3. **Address confidence separately if needed.** Test small legal-action-aware label smoothing (for example 0.05, an unvalidated starting value). Alternatively fit a post-hoc temperature on separate calibration games and evaluate on untouched games. Temperature scaling changes confidence without changing argmax accuracy and does not fix training gradients. Existing inference temperature 0.9 sharpens predictions; it should not be assumed optimal from these calibration results.
4. **If gradient drift persists, isolate normalization.** A lower LR for BN affine parameters or a GroupNorm ablation can test targeted hypotheses. A 0.1x affine LR would be a proposed starting point, not an established optimum. Exempting normalization/bias from weight decay is a reasonable control, but our prior plain-model result was nearly neutral; fixed affine parameters were worse. Do not present either intervention as a proven fix.
5. **Keep clipping as a guardrail.** Raising the threshold only changes what is clipped. With AdamW, clipping gradients is not a direct bound on the subsequent parameter update. Judge loss, calibration, actual relative updates, and layer-wise gradient distributions together.

The preceding post-hoc analysis made no new training runs or production-default changes; the later follow-up below includes a new training run. Derived checkpoint diagnostics are saved in late_training_diagnostics.json.

###### Interpretation of the faster-decay result

**The faster decay reduced gradient tails but did not fix probability overfitting.** Over the identical
40,001–80,000-update window, clipping fell from 12.84% to 2.86%, and the maximum pre-clip norm fell from
14.94 to 9.35. Mean pre-clip gradient L2 was almost unchanged (4.060 versus 4.039), so this should not
be described as eliminating large gradients generally. Clipping still occurred on 5.0% of the final 5k updates.

Final raw accuracy increased by approximately 0.43 percentage points (22.22% to 22.65%), and final legal
accuracy by 0.44 points (23.07% to 23.51%). However, raw NLL worsened from 3.6239 to 3.6600 and legal NLL
from 3.3423 to 3.3815. Legal ECE was essentially unchanged (0.1403 versus 0.1424). The lower training LR
therefore did not deliver the hoped-for generalization/calibration improvement.

The best saved raw NLLs are nearly tied: 3.5724 at 40k in the reference versus 3.5687 at 25k with faster
decay. Best saved legal NLLs are also close: 3.2078 at 20k versus 3.1999 at 15k. The new run has sixteen
evaluations rather than four, so these tiny best-checkpoint differences are not evidence of superiority.
On the original four shared checkpoints, the previous schedule has better best raw and legal NLL.
The primary endpoint comparisons above use identical 80k budgets.

Several internal statistics improved without improving NLL. Final dense weight L2 was 39.50 versus
65.71, policy weight L2 837.19 versus 1226.11, and the last residual branch BN gamma median 0.298 versus
0.137. Top-four trunk activity share was 53.6% versus 65.7%; dense activity share remained about 11.9%
in both. Dense dormant fraction stayed 7.8%. Smaller norms and more distributed trunk activity should
not be equated with better probability predictions.

Actual late relative updates also decreased. Mean update/weight L2 for the stem fell from 0.0980% to
0.0286%, dense layer from 0.0964% to 0.0309%, policy from 0.00577% to 0.00176%, and last branch BN from
0.0743% to 0.0119%. These are means pooled across the same late window. All parameters and gradients
remained finite.

Changing LR also changes cumulative AdamW decay because each step multiplies updated parameters by
(1 - LR * weight_decay). Ignoring gradient updates, the accumulated multiplier is approximately 0.475
for the old schedule and 0.666 for the faster schedule. Thus the intervention changes both step sizes
and cumulative shrinkage; the results do not isolate these as separate causal mechanisms, and the BN
gamma difference must not be attributed solely to one of them.

**Revised conclusion:** sustained high LR was not sufficient to explain the validation-NLL deterioration.
The follow-up supports treating gradient-tail control and probability overfitting as distinct objectives.
Faster decay is a tradeoff: modestly higher move accuracy and fewer clipped updates, with no NLL or
calibration gain in this seed. Do not promote it as a universal fix or change production defaults on that claim.

For probability quality, retain legal-NLL-based checkpoint selection; the best legal-NLL checkpoint here is
15k, not the 80k accuracy checkpoint. The next targeted intervention would address confidence directly,
for example a controlled legal-action-aware label-smoothing test, or post-hoc temperature calibration on
separate calibration/evaluation games. Neither has been run in this follow-up. For residual optimization
questions, normalization-specific controls remain separate experiments rather than established remedies.

All 41 tests passed before launch. Actual batch hashes match the reference at all shared checkpoints;
warmup LR traces match exactly and the new final LR is 1e-5. The 5k model tensors reproduce exactly.
An independent RNG replay also verified at 10k and 15k that added evaluations consumed no training randomness.
The full validation calibration comparison and all sixteen checkpoint metrics are retained in JSON files.

##### Full-data residual run 27846286

Completed 50 epochs in 2.59 hours, 2,090,250 optimizer updates. Model: 348,081
parameters, 16 channels, hidden size 64, three residual blocks, convolutional
BatchNorm, dropout 0.1, default initialization. All 55,250 training games
(5,350,942 positions); 6,141 validation games (595,179 positions).

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Best full-validation raw accuracy | 27.81%, epoch 47 |
| Best fixed-probe legal accuracy | 28.77%, epoch 43; saved best_policy.pt |
| Best full-validation raw NLL | 2.8876, epoch 49 |
| Final raw accuracy / NLL | 27.79% / 2.8897 |
| Final training NLL | 2.9825, measured with dropout active |
| Final legal-probe accuracy / NLL | 28.54% / 2.7003 |
| Clipped updates | 100% from epoch 4 onward |
| Pre-clip global gradient median | 3.01 at epoch 1; 36.25 at epoch 50 |
| Largest gradient observed | 522.02, epoch 15 |
| Final last-trunk activation zeros | 91.57% |
| Final last-trunk dormant channels | 9/16, relative activity threshold on 512 observations |
| Single-channel share of last-trunk mean absolute activity | 98.39% |
| Final dense ReLU dormant features | 2/64 |
| Final dense top-four activity share | 12.59% |

Validation loss improved from 3.1168 to 2.8897, with its best at epoch 49.
This is not the pilot's late validation-loss overfitting pattern. Training loss
is measured with dropout active, whereas validation is evaluated with dropout
inactive; their ordering does not establish leakage or lack of learning.

The internal problem persists at full data scale. First-layer ReLU has no
dormant channels; dense features remain relatively balanced. Concentration is
strongest near the end of the convolutional residual trunk. Activity share is
not causal contribution: a channel-ablation evaluation is needed to establish
how much predictions depend on that channel.

Largest final median layer gradients are last-block norm2 (18.34), stem norm
(17.55), second-block norm2 (13.01), dense layer (12.76), first-block norm2
(11.35). BatchNorm affine parameters are prominent. Stem gamma median is
0.0421 and last-block norm2 gamma median 0.00933, while one last-block gamma
is 1.955. Dense and policy weight L2 norms are approximately 386 and 2,864.
Running variances are small in several interior blocks, but finite; these
alone do not establish broken statistics. All recorded gradients are finite.
Actual relative updates shrink with LR; dense median relative update drops
from 0.001738 in epoch 1 to 0.000001336 in epoch 50. High raw gradients do not
mean all parameters receive runaway updates. Global clipping rescales every
layer's raw gradient; Adam's adaptive moments mean that this rescaling cannot
be read as a proportional reduction in actual parameter updates.

A plausible mechanism is scale imbalance among normalized trunk features and
the dense classifier. This is a hypothesis, not a causal diagnosis. Literature
shows normalization and regularization interact through parameter scale and
effective learning rate, but does not prove the cause in this AdamW run:
https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.05350
https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.05101

Long-run decay exposure differs substantially from the short pilots: the
counterfactual decay-only multiplier over this run is about 2.60e-5. This
ignores all loss gradients and is not an estimate of actual parameter shrinkage.
It motivates controlling duration when testing regularization, rather than
assuming unchanged weight_decay means an identical effect across budgets.

The earlier plain 64/256 CNN achieved raw accuracy 30.98% and NLL 2.5810 in
8 epochs. This residual run does not beat it on these metrics, despite more
updates. It has approximately 6.2 times fewer parameters, different architecture,
dropout and schedule, so this is not a controlled residual-vs-plain comparison.
The best legal accuracy comes from a fixed 8,192-position probe, not all held-out
positions; epoch 43 is not proven best on the full legal validation set.

Next: evaluate the saved best models on matched held-out games and measure
sensitivity to ablating the dominant trunk channel. If testing a training fix,
run a matched residual baseline versus excluding normalization affine and
bias parameters from decay, long enough to reproduce the epoch-2/3 onset.
The earlier short pilot found little benefit from that exemption, so it is a
hypothesis test, not an established solution. Do not increase clipping threshold
or launch another 50-epoch run solely on the basis of the current diagnostics.
More data improved held-out learning but did not remove feature concentration.

##### Head-to-head: residual versus best full CNN

Played 100 games using evaluate.py, alternating colors (50 each), 180+2 clocks,
max 1000 plies, sampling temperature 0.9, shared current observation-based move
filtering. Residual: best_policy.pt from run 27846286, epoch 43, selected by
legal accuracy on 8192 fixed held-out positions. Full CNN: best_policy.pt from
27800942, epoch 8, selected by raw validation loss (also best raw accuracy).
Original checkpoints were preserved; evaluation used separate frozen bundles.

Residual: 32 wins, 68 losses, zero draws. As white: 14/50 wins; as black:
18/50 wins. No bot failures. All games terminated with King capturable, the
fog-of-war referee's terminal condition. Mean length 63.6 plies (12–139).
Elapsed 878.2 seconds. Approximate 95% Wilson interval for the residual win
probability in this matchup: 23.7%–41.7%, assuming independent games.
This is one stochastic matchup with default starting boards, not a broad
strength rating or a causal test of the training issues.

The full CNN wins clearly in this series. The residual's 348081 parameters
are substantially fewer than the plain CNN's 2146817; architecture, dropout,
training duration and checkpoint criterion also differ. Thus this comparison
does not establish residual architecture as worse, or capacity as the only
cause of the gap.

A useful next capacity test is channels=64, hidden_size=256, residual_blocks=3,
dropout=0.1: 2332353 parameters, close to the plain CNN's capacity. Keep the
remaining recipe fixed for that experiment and inspect early checkpoints
before committing to another long run. A larger residual is a capacity test,
not an established cure for the normalization gradient / feature concentration
problem. It may reproduce those problems. No larger training run was launched.

#### Retired snapshot usage notes: `out/experiments/arena-small-residual-vs-full-cnn-100games/full_cnn/README.md`

# Feedforward neural bot

This bot owns its `policy.pt` and uses the model definitions, observation tracker,
and arena protocol implementation in `starters/shared/`.

From the repository root:

```sh
.venv/bin/python starters/neural/bot.py
```

For matches, use `bash starters/neural/run.sh` as a referee bot command.
Activate `.venv` first so `run.sh` and `build.sh` use the installed dependencies.
`build.sh` validates the checkpoint. The bot uses CPU inference, samples legal moves
from `softmax(logits / 0.9)`, and chooses queen promotions. Recurrent memory
updates once per observation and resets each game.

Train with `python training/train.py --model-type feedforward`.
The run saves its own best and final checkpoints under `out/`; it does not
replace this bot's weights. Use `--output` with a fresh checkpoint path for an
additional export. See `training/CLUSTER.md` for GPU cluster instructions.
To evaluate against the other CNN bot, run:

```sh
.venv/bin/python evaluate.py neural neural_recurrent
```

The evaluator plays 20 games, alternating colors, and reports results from the
first bot's perspective. Both checkpoints are frozen for the series.

Create a standalone arena submission with shared code included:

```sh
.venv/bin/python starters/shared/bundle.py starters/neural --output build/neural
```

Use a fresh output directory. ZIP the contents of `build/neural/` for submission.
The bundled `build.sh` and `run.sh` work without the repository. PyTorch and
python-chess must be available in the runtime; initialization must fit 15 seconds.


#### Retired snapshot usage notes: `out/experiments/arena-small-residual-vs-full-cnn-100games/full_cnn/shared/README.md`

# Shared neural bot code

- `model.py`: feedforward and recurrent architectures, observation encoding,
  and the training interface. Training datasets remain in `training/`.
- `moves.py`: observation history, legal move generation, and visible king safety.
- `policy_bot.py`: persistent arena protocol and checkpoint inference, sampling
  from the legal-move softmax at temperature 0.9 (fresh randomness each game).
- `bundle.py`: packages one bot with a frozen checkpoint and shared runtime.

Each bot directory owns its entrypoint, checkpoint, and launch/build scripts.
Local entrypoints import this directory. Bundled submissions import their own
included `shared/` directory. A future PPO bot can reuse these modules and expose
the same `run.sh` interface, with its own inference code when needed.

Move tracking uses the root `referee.py` as the canonical source of game rules.
The bundler includes that module in generated standalone submissions.

Before sampling, move generation simulates each candidate and filters moves
that leave the king attacked by visible enemy pieces along known clear paths.
Hidden attackers and unknown blockers remain uncertain. If no candidate passes,
the bot retains the legal candidates so it can still submit a move. The referee
rules are unchanged; FOW castling checks only final-position safety here.

New training runs can use LeakyReLU in the encoder, with activation and slope
stored in checkpoint metadata. The bot reads those settings; checkpoints that
omit them use the historical ReLU architecture. Weight shapes and encoder layer
indices are unchanged, so existing checkpoints retain their original behavior.

### Artifact policy after consolidation

`EXPERIMENT_HISTORY.md` is the sole narrative findings record. Raw metrics, split manifests, checkpoint files and plots remain evidence under `out/experiments/`. New local training and evaluation runs use descriptive names, with `-repeat2`, `-repeat3`, etc. when a name is already used. Explicit output/run-directory overrides remain supported. The residual-decay runner appends generated findings here instead of recreating per-run reports. The artifact_migration.json file records relocations and hashes of retired reports; it is provenance, not a second findings report. New cluster jobs save under out/experiments; the in-flight medium residual job retains its old server output path until completion.

## 28. Completed full-data medium residual: job 27890681 (2026-11-04)

This resolves the pending medium residual experiment described in stage25. Numerical evidence is in `/Users/jesuscaraball0/code/school_code/67980/fow/out/experiments/residual-medium-27890681/metrics.json`, checkpoint inspection and comparative aggregates in `/Users/jesuscaraball0/code/school_code/67980/fow/out/experiments/residual-medium-27890681/analysis-summary.json`. No new training or arena games were run for this analysis.

### Recipe, data and comparison controls

The 32-channel /128-hidden, three-block residual CNN has **850,785 parameters**. It completed all **50 epochs /2,090,250 updates**, in **13,678.55 seconds (3.80 hours)**. Small residual baseline:348,081 parameters, same 50 epochs and2,090,250 updates,2.59hours. This is2.44× the parameters and1.47× the measured wall time in these cluster runs; hardware equivalence is not independently established, so wall-time scaling is descriptive rather than a controlled throughput law.

Both use full data (5,350,942 training positions from55,250 usable games;595,179 validation positions from6,141 usable games), seed 7980, batch 128, default initialization, ReLU, convolutional BN, hidden dropout0.1, AdamW(.9,.99), eps1e-8, weight decay.01, global clip 5, warmup 5,820 updates1e-4→1e-3 and cosine decay over the remaining50epochbudget to1e-5. Saved settings match except model dimensions/parameter count and run-specific paths. Ordered split filenames match the small residual and plain CNN. Split manifests list55,301/6,144 replay files, whereas datasets count55,250/6,141 usable games: ReplayDataset increments games only for files containing examples, so these are not contradictory counts. Same seed and data do not make different-width initializations a paired-seed average or prove identical minibatch tensor hashes; no such hashes were recorded by this production trainer.

### Prediction results

| Model | Parameters | Epochs | Final full-val raw NLL | Final full-val raw accuracy | Best saved legal-probe accuracy | Saved best epoch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small residual16/64 |348,081|50|2.889692|27.7926%|28.7720%|43|
| Medium residual32/128 |850,785|50|2.613601|31.1537%|31.5186%|49|
| Plain full CNN64/256+BN |2,147,073|8|2.580976|30.9801%|31.2744% at its saved epoch 8|8|

“Best saved legal accuracy” uses the same fixed8,192-position probe, not the595,179-position full validation set. The plain CNN's saved best criterion was raw NLL, whereas the residuals select legal-probe accuracy. The table does not imply the plain CNN was selected by legal accuracy or that its best legal-probe accuracy across all epochs has been searched. Final and saved-best states differ in residual models.

The medium model's final raw accuracy improves by **3.3610 percentage points** over the small residual; raw NLL improves by **0.276092**. Best legal-probe accuracy rises by **2.7466points**. This supports a capacity benefit for this recipe; the earlier small model was not sufficient to characterize all residual models.

Versus the plain CNN, final raw accuracy is only **0.1736points higher**, while raw NLL is **0.032624 worse**, despite50epochs versus8 (6.25× optimizer updates). This is a metric/compute tradeoff, not a decisive residual victory. At the same eight-epoch exposure, the medium residual had raw NLL 2.829686 and accuracy 28.2238%, versus the plain CNN's 2.580976 and 30.9801%; it needed substantially more training to close that gap. Best-legal-probe accuracy is0.2441points higher than the plain CNN's epoch 8 probe, an exploratory comparison after repeated validation use; correlated positions and one seed limit significance claims. No new playing-strength comparison has been run, so neither the previous32–68 small-residual result nor imitation accuracy establishes medium-residual strength.

**Checkpoint choice:** `best_policy.pt` is epoch 49, legal-probe accuracy31.5186%, raw accuracy31.15315%, raw NLL2.613681, legal-probe NLL2.514548. `final_policy.pt` is epoch 50, raw accuracy31.15365%, raw NLL2.613601, legal-probe accuracy31.2622%, legal NLL 2.508901. Thus final has slightly better raw NLL/accuracy and legal NLL, while the saved best is correctly chosen by higher probe accuracy. Differences in raw accuracy between epochs49and50 are tiny (three full-validation correct predictions).

### Learning trajectory: not ordinary late validation overfitting

Validation raw NLL goes2.8524→2.6136 and raw accuracy27.70%→31.15%; the best recorded full-validation NLL and raw accuracy are at epoch 50. Validation has noticeable transients (e.g. epoch 13NLL3.0532 and epoch 30NLL2.9562) but late performance continues improving. Training NLL is2.6614 at epoch 49 and2.6706 at epoch 50, measured with active dropout; validation uses dropout off. The final training-loss increase and extreme gradient maximum are observations, not proof of causal divergence. The train/validation loss ordering does not by itself indicate leakage. Increasing size has not produced the classic late validation-NLL overfitting pattern in this full-data run.

### Optimization problem persists and rare tails worsen

Clipped updates:9.86% in epoch 1,65.02% in epoch 2,99.29% in epoch 3, **100% from epoch 4 through50**. Global pre-clip median is2.93 initially,14.49 at epoch 3,44.63 finally; finalp95is110.34. Compared with the small residual's final median36.25,p9581.98, this is a larger gradient burden; width also changes the number of parameters, so raw L2 norms are not dimension-normalized health scores.

Rare maximum gradients are markedly larger: **69,942.66 at epoch 50**, versus small model's overall maximum522.02. Other medium epochs include6,704.75(epoch 20),10,321.11(epoch 24),8,378.89(epoch 28),65,786.45(epoch 30). All recorded gradients and inspected best/final parameters/buffers are finite; maximum post-clip norm is5.00000143, consistent with float32 reduction tolerance. The largest50th-epoch per-layer maxima include stemBN48,676.14, first-blockBN2 27,166.30, second-blockBN2 21,981.56, last-blockBN2 20,031.33 and stemconv15,025.81. Typical final median gradients are led by second-blockBN2 26.39, last-blockBN2 20.27, last-blockBN1 18.91, last-blockconv1 10.99, last-blockconv2 10.53. This is not exclusively a classifier-head problem.

Clipping kept raw gradient norms bounded after rescaling, but does not directly bound AdamW parameter changes. Actual sampled relative-update medians decrease withLR: stem0.001474→0.00001460, dense0.001622→0.000001555, policy0.0001375→0.0000002658. They are not sampled at every update, so these summaries cannot certify the exact optimizer update on the rare spike steps. The model kept learning; calling it numerically divergent or claiming clipping solved it would both overstate the evidence.

### Feature concentration remains severe in the late trunk

Exact activation reductions cover512 validation observations, not the whole split.

| Final diagnostic | Small residual16/64 | Medium residual32/128 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stem ReLU dormant channels |0/16|0/32|
| Last-trunk zero activation fraction |91.57%|96.71%|
| Last-trunk relatively dormant channels |9/16(56.25%)|21/32(65.625%)|
| Last-trunk top-channel activity share |98.39%|89.68%|
| Last-trunk top-four share |99.36%|98.10%|
| Dense relatively dormant features |2/64(3.125%)|13/128(10.156%)|
| Dense top-four activity share |12.59%|18.17%|

One dominant trunk channel remains, although its share is lower than in the small residual. Dormancy and sparsity increased; dense activity became less balanced on these measures. Because widths differ, a fixed top-four share has a different uniform baseline (6.25% versus3.125% in the dense layer). These are mixed internal changes, not a uniform “healthier” or “collapsed” verdict. Activity share is not causal importance or feature-information rank; channel ablation and standardized covariance tests have not been run for this model.

The last trunk already had top-channel share67.47% after epoch 1 and90.45% after epoch 3. By epoch 10 it was94.20%; the final89.68% is a partial reduction rather than late recovery to balanced channels. Second-block activity is also concentrated (finaltopchannel55.01%,topfour92.45%). Stem and first-block channels remain much more distributed.

Best/final checkpoint inspection shows small learned BN scales in many channels: final stemgamma median.04042; lastbranchBN2 gamma median.03280 with maximum1.08949. Final lastbranchBN1 running variance minimum3.54e-5,median7.65e-4; lastbranchBN2 minimum.00208,median.06223. These are finite and do not alone prove bad buffers or identify a causal mechanism. Dense weightL2~523.86,policy~3261.42; policy softmax has a common-offset invariance, so larger norms are not by themselves a prediction-quality test.

### Takeaways and next decisions

1. **Capacity helped predictions.** The medium residual substantially closes the small model's validation gap while using~60% fewer parameters than the plainfull CNN. The small model's weakness was not evidence that residual connections are inherently inferior.
2. **Capacity did not cure the internal problem.** Sustained clipping, strongly concentrated late-trunk activity, small BN scales and very large rare gradient tails persist. Do not infer that making it larger again is a fix.
3. **The medium result is competitive, not an established overall winner.** Raw accuracy is slightly higher than the plain CNN, NLL worse, training exposure much larger, and playing strength unmeasured. The original Adam50epoch feedforward run also exists with different settings; this comparison does not claim best-ever accuracy across all historical runs.
4. **Keep the requested accuracy-based checkpoint.** Epoch49 is the exported best; retain final separately. Since selection uses8,192 positions, avoid treating a small probe difference as proof of full-distribution improvement.
5. **Next useful check is the existing arena evaluator:** medium best versus small residual best and the prior full CNN best, with equal colors and identical inference settings. This analysis did not run those games. Before another widening/long training run, isolate one optimization intervention at this same medium capacity. Normalization/bias decay exemption is still only a candidate: the prior plain-model subset test was nearly neutral and fixed affine was worse. No causal remedy has yet been demonstrated.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| White |30|19|1|61.0%|
| Black |24|26|0|48.0%|
| **Total** |**54**|**45**|**1**|**54.5%**|

Winrate is54%; score with draw=0.5 is54.5%. Reasons:99 King capturable,1 threefold repetition. Both bots had0 failures. Mean game length **68.12plies**, min6,max150. Total parallel wall time **550.51seconds (9.18minutes)**; parallel timing is not directly comparable with a serial evaluation's per-game wall time.

Among99 decisive games, medium wins54: **54.55%**, approximate95%Wilson interval **44.75%–64.00%** assuming independent games. The interval includes50%; the observed narrow lead does **not** establish statistically convincing superiority. This interval is for decisive-game win probability, not a confidence interval for the draw-adjusted score. There is no held-out opponent population, Elo estimate, multiple-seed model comparison, or opening suite here.

### Interpretation

1. **The medium residual is competitive with this full CNN checkpoint.** It has a small observed lead,54.5% score, at~60%fewer parameters. We cannot call it definitively stronger based on100 games.
2. **It closes the gap observed for the small residual.** The prior small-residual series scored32%, versus54.5%here against the identical opponent checkpoint. The two series use fresh random games, and the models differ in width/initialization. This supports the practical benefit of the medium recipe; it is not an isolated multi-seed causal estimate of capacity.
3. **Predictive accuracy and playing strength now both suggest near parity, rather than a clear residual victory.** The medium has slightly higher raw imitation accuracy, worse raw NLL and much more training exposure than the plainCNN. A near-even arena result is compatible with these mixed prediction metrics.
4. **Competitive performance does not negate the optimization diagnostics.** All-update clipping and late-trunk concentration remain observed in the saved training run; these games do not prove that those issues are harmless or causally limit strength. They also show that the concerning internal statistics did not prevent the model from playing competitively.
5. This result alone does not justify another size increase or further training. More games could resolve a small strength difference; targeted training changes remain separate hypotheses. No continuation training was performed.

The SSOT now includes this additional100-game comparison, retaining both50-game raw batch summaries and the combined summary. Earlier statements that medium playing strength was unmeasured describe the pre-evaluation state and are superseded by this section.

## 49. Boosted CNN: server pretraining infrastructure (2026-11-05; implemented, not launched)

User explicitly requested a new boosted CNN variant, pretraining on all historical games for50 epochs with past hyperparameters, and cluster sync/submission/log commands. They selected20-turn history + last-seen + age. This supersedes the cancelled raw4-frame prototype as the intended input design. No local pretraining, PPO run, cluster job or new automation was started for this task. The only optimizer steps run locally were tiny temporary unit-test fixtures.

### Architecture and input contract

Variant name: boosted_cnn; starter directory starters/boosted_cnn; canonical future PPO identity boosted-cnn-c32-h128-f4004a979d for the configured model. Uses the previous medium residual CNN:32 convolutional channels,128 hidden features,3 residual blocks, convolutional BN,ReLU,dropout0.1. Input expansion increases parameter count from850785 to1370625; hidden/trunk dimensions are not otherwise enlarged. Existing models and variant IDs remain compatible. New inputs use ordinary framework Conv2d initialization across the entire input layer; there is no custom He reinitialization or zero-initialized boosted feature bank. The cancelled raw-frame pilot retains its distinct matched-control initialization.

Boosted_v1 features total1819 spatial planes:

| Component | Planes | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
|20 own-turn records |1800|Each record90 planes, newest first; missing records zero-padded|
|Within each record: observed board |14|Original piece/color/empty/unknown encoding at that own decision|
|Within each record: previous completed own move |73|56 ray classes,8 knight classes,9 underpromotion classes, anchored at origin; absent at first own turn|
|Within each record: observed captures |2|Where we last captured an enemy; where enemy last captured one of ours, inferred from allowed views/actions|
|Within each record: own color |1|White1/black0 on valid records|
|Current own castling rights |2|Known kingside/queenside rights from existing tracker|
|Last-seen contents |14|Last actually observed contents of each square, including known empty versus never-seen unknown|
|Age |1|Plies since that square was visible, capped254 and divided254|
|Ever-seen |1|Separates never-seen from old saturated-age observations|
|Current visibility |1|Which squares are currently visible|

History records advance once per own decision (20 turns, usually40 plies), rather than the cancelled4-view every-ply stack. Last-seen and age update on every observation received, including opponent-turn observations. Age0 means visible now. Last-seen pieces are stale evidence, not asserted current truth. Only actual earlier own moves are encoded; the target action is recorded after its input has been emitted. Own capture metadata includes observable en-passant captures. No sensing-action or illegal-attempt feedback is fabricated because our game does not supply those RBC-specific channels. No unseen opponent actions or hidden board fields enter the features.

Implementation: starters/shared/boosted_features.py; shared checkpoint-compatible Policy/create_policy; imitation dataset/probes; in-process PPO agents; standalone policy_bot and bundled arena runtime. Model kind stays feedforward with model_config.boosted=true, so existing PPO/evaluation/export machinery can use it after imitation pretraining. There is one separate canonical RL file for this variant when PPO is eventually requested; original full/residual weights are untouched.

### Full-data storage and training recipe

training/boosted_dataset.py builds disk-backed compact per-decision rows, not full float history stacks. One row203 bytes, plus4-byte game-start index and2-byte label; approximately1.2GiB for6million positions. __getitem__ gathers up to20 same-player records using within-game indices and constructs1592 uint8 packed tokens. Feature planes are expanded only for a batch on the selected device. This avoids hundreds of gigabytes of repeated float history materialization. Cache at out/cache/boosted-v1 is versioned/keyed by ordered source paths, sizes and timestamps, protected by a file lock, and committed with a manifest only after successful preprocessing. Interrupted preprocessing rebuilds safely. No new dependency is required beyond existing training requirements.

training/boosted_cnn.sbatch requests the existing mit_normal_gpu allocation:1GPU,4CPUs,32GiB RAM,6hours. It activates existing .venv-cnn and checks CUDA. Full dataset,seed7980,90/10 game-level split, no train/validation file limits. Training settings exactly match the previous residual_cnn.sbatch, verified by parsing/comparing all flags other than the new --boosted flag:

-50epochs,batch128,global grad clip5,default initialization.
-AdamW LRstart1e-4,peak1e-3,minimum1e-5;5820 warmup updates then cosine decay across all50 epochs.
-Betas0.9/0.99,epsilon1e-8,weight decay0.01.
-Best checkpoint maximizes legal top1 on8192 fixed held-out moves; raw validation metrics cover the entire validation split; earlier checkpoint wins ties.
-Existing losses/LR/gradients/update ratios, activation diagnostics/final per-layer weight+activation histograms, plots, split manifests and epoch-boundary optimizer/RNG resume retained.

Fresh outputs: out/experiments/boosted-cnn-JOBID; logs logs/boosted-cnn-JOBID.out/.err. Initial feature encoding progress is in stderr. Wall time for1819-channel inputs is not established; no claim50 epochs fits6hours. If the allocation expires, resume the original last_policy.pt with a new sbatch allocation; it keeps the original run directory, optimizer/schedule and selected best. If no epoch checkpoint exists yet, resubmit fresh and reuse/rebuild the cache. No unconditional automatic resubmission is installed.

Together these exercise the74-test current suite's coverage, including dataset/live/probe token parity, future-target/hidden-board isolation, captures/promotion encoding, padding/reset, no cross-game/side history, cache reuse, tiny temporary imitation/resume/PPO integration, standalone bundled protocol play for both colors and old canonical variant compatibility. ### Selected-checkpoint imitation metrics

The selection criterion remains highest legal top1 on8192 fixed held-out positions, not minimum full-validation loss. Boosted selects epoch50; old residual selects49. Full-validation raw metrics below use all595179 held-out moves. Legal metrics use the fixed8192-position probe, without conflating legality with the observation-based king-safety filter. These are imitation metrics, not win rates.

| Metric | Residual best49 | Boosted best50 |

| Training cross entropy |2.66135|2.61881|

At epoch48, the matched epoch comparison is34.853% versus31.145% raw top1 and2.47667 versus2.61503 validation NLL, so the advantage does not depend solely on best-checkpoint selection. The legal probe is a small correlated subset of moves and not8192 independent games; do not infer a game-win confidence interval from it.

|1|3.17478|2.71872|31.182%|30.823%|

Learning continues late, but at diminishing gains: full-validation top1 adds.470points from40→50 and.032points from49→50. Validation loss remains improving;50epochs does not establish convergence. This is not the classic training-loss-down/validation-loss-up pattern of sustained overfitting. Training loss includes dropout and train-mode BN, while validation uses eval mode, so train>validation is not paradoxical. The last-epoch training CE rises despite improving validation; raw gradient spikes and feature scale drift justify caution rather than treating the training-loss jump alone as generalization collapse.

### Optimization: the old concern persists, with a heavier extreme tail

At boosted epoch50, pre-clipping global gradient L2 mean62.915,median34.769,p95=63.941,max278925.19. Old residual best49:mean53.251,median44.743,p95=111.486,max739.91. Boosted has lower typical gradients (median/p95), but much larger rare spikes. The largest boosted epoch-level maximum is289807.125 at46; the residual's run-wide maximum is69942.656 at50. Comparing selected-epoch maxima alone would obscure that the residual also has outliers.

Clipping affects10.20% of updates at epoch1, exceeds99% by epoch4, and reaches100% in later epochs. At50 all41805 updates are clipped; post-clipping global norm averages5.00000. Every recorded global gradient nonfinite count is0 across50epochs, and final weights/recorded activation statistics are finite. Clipping controls the update input norm; it does not eliminate the cause of scale drift, and clipping frequency alone is not evidence that training diverged.

| Boosted epoch50 layer | Mean pre-clip L2 | p95 pre-clip | Maximum pre-clip | Mean post-clip L2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
|Input convolution encoder.0|4.983|2.251|38485.38|.255|
|Input BN encoder.norm0|27.560|11.301|253943.22|1.100|
|Last residual conv2|5.501|8.542|2531.48|.664|
|Last residual BN2|18.499|27.457|37997.47|1.727|
|Dense encoder.5|10.443|12.018|287.40|1.428|
|Policy linear head|19.107|20.605|43.47|2.639|

The mean exceeding p95 in early layers reflects rare severe outliers. The worst input-BN spike shows that the issue is not confined to the final dense/head layers. Sampled actual optimizer update/parameter L2 medians at50 are1.083e-5/input convolution,1.549e-6/dense and2.796e-7/policy; respective p95 values1.181e-5,1.692e-6,3.061e-7. These are small late actual relative updates, despite alarming raw gradients. Sampling every100steps can miss rare updates. Policy gradient magnitude is much larger than in the old residual (mean19.107 vs.17325), but global clipping, weight scale and Adam preconditioning prevent interpreting that ratio as an equally large parameter-update ratio.

### Activation and weight histograms: mixed health, not wholesale collapse

Statistics use512 fixed validation observations, not all held-out games. First ReLU encoder.1 has56.48%zeros,mean.0128,std.0210; zeros alone are normal for ReLU. The residual trunk becomes very sparse: block0 output81.06%zeros,block1 output91.85%,final block95.53%. Final-block dormant-channel fraction is68.75% using the recorded relative-activity threshold; these are activity diagnostics, not proof those channels are permanently dead on every state.

Final-trunk largest-channel activity share improves from89.67%/old residual best to77.48%/boosted; top4 still account for99.17%. Dense output encoder.6 goes the other way: its largest unit contributes96.37% of total mean absolute activation, versus7.78% in the old residual. Its overall zero fraction is54.76%,similar to residual54.49%,which demonstrates why aggregate zero fraction alone misses scale concentration. Dense std grows.368/epoch1→1.478/20→6.908/40→21.739/50. Dominant channel72 has mean238.199,std65.004 and is positive on every sampled observation. This is substantial feature-scale drift, not a clean bill of architectural health.

Final policy logits have mean−555.13,std141.03 on these observations; the policy weight histogram is strongly negative/skewed rather than a requirement-satisfying Gaussian. Negative logits themselves are harmless: softmax depends on differences, and a state-dependent common offset cancels exactly. The outgoing weights for dense72 have mean−2.16131 and across-action std.03724,versus median across-action std2.96459 for policy columns. Much of that huge unit therefore contributes a common logit offset. A normally distributed weight histogram is not itself the learning objective, and activation mass is not predictive importance.

To test function rather than infer from histograms, the selected boosted50 checkpoint was evaluated locally in eval/inference mode on the same8192 held-out probe and then with dense channel72 set to zero by a removable forward hook. No weights, BN buffers or checkpoint files were updated:

| CPU inference probe | Intact | Dense72 zeroed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
|Legal top1|35.022%|34.277%|
|Legal NLL|2.42006|2.48208|
|Raw top1|34.875%|34.058%|
|Legal probability mass|89.439%|88.972%|

Removing the unit costs.745percentage points of legal accuracy and.06202NLL. It is useful, but96%activation share emphatically does not mean96%of the policy's decisions come from that unit. This inference intervention is an out-of-distribution ablation, not a retrained smaller model. CPU intact legal accuracy differs from the saved CUDA probe by2/8192 positions (.0244points); NLL differs.000054. Small backend rounding differences with large logits are a plausible explanation, not a tested attribution. Report saved CUDA results for the training comparison and local CPU results for the paired intervention.

The value output histogram (mean5.33,std1.43) is **not a learned outcome predictor**: imitation only supervised policy loss. Existing PPO initialization zeroes the untrained value head for a fresh supervised checkpoint. Do not carry this arbitrary value scale into an interpretation of critic quality.

### Takeaways and next experiment

1. The combined boosted representation/model is a better historical move predictor than the prior medium residual under matched split and optimization budget. It supplies a promising starting actor; this does not establish superior live play, history-specific causality, or robustness to new opponents.
2. History did not cure gradient clipping, trunk concentration, or dense feature-scale drift. Nevertheless, loss/accuracy improve and the unit ablation argues against describing the entire actor as collapsed. More architecture changes or another long imitation run are not justified solely by histogram appearance.
3. **Proceed next to a short monitored PPO experiment, preceded by a frozen-game benchmark**, rather than immediately committing a long blind RL run. Use boosted best_policy.pt (epoch50; identical to latest/final). Benchmark against the supervised residual and established RL opponents with balanced colors and fixed seeds, then train boosted against a balanced fixed mixture of full latest2200 and residual saved-best1200. Preserve those opponents; update boosted alone initially, so opponent drift does not obscure its own progress. Do not use residual latest2200 as the only strong opponent: stage45 found it had regressed against its incumbent.
4. A400-update initial PPO budget is a reasonable next experiment, using the established lambda1 recipe as the starting reference, with evaluations at0 and regular intervals. Track fixed-opponent score, rewards/draws/length, KL/entropy/ratio clip, global gradient clipping, MC outcome RMSE/EV and feature scales. Keep the original supervised file separate and the new boosted canonical RL file plus embedded best. Stop/reassess if score or critic transfer deteriorates;400 is a diagnostic budget, not a promised convergence horizon. Critic initialization and the high-scale shared representation deserve monitoring; zero initialization does not guarantee a well-conditioned critic after its first updates.
5. Hold PSRO until there is evidence that this third actor learns useful complementary behavior. No boosted PPO, arena benchmark or PSRO run was launched by this analysis, and no new game-win metric is claimed here.

New numerical evidence: `out/experiments/boosted-cnn-28018186/completed-run-analysis/snapshot-analysis.json`, including full per-epoch layer gradients/update ratios/activity summaries and SHA256s for best/last; derived comparison plot `training-comparison.png`. Original metrics and checkpoints are untouched. Final server-generated per-layer histograms remain in `histograms.json`, `activations/` and `weights/`.

## 55. Boosted outcome CNN: matched joint-pretraining infrastructure (2026-11-06; implemented, not launched)

User requested a new boosted_outcome_cnn variant using the medium residual backbone and same full-data server pretraining setup,adding game-outcome prediction alongside next-move prediction. This is a controlled training-objective comparison against boosted-cnn-28018186,not a bigger network or a new feature design. Model:32channels,128hidden,3residual blocks,convBN,ReLU,dropout.1;1819boosted input planes;1370625parameters. Input features retain20own-turn observation/action histories,last-seen contents,age,visibility/ever-seen,own castling/color/capture metadata. Game state means available observations/known metadata,not unseen board contents. Final result is a **target only**,never an input. No full-data local training,server job,PPO or automation was launched.

New starter `starters/boosted_outcome_cnn`,same shared inference/game contract. Training flag `--boosted-outcome` implies boosted inputs and sets model_config.outcome_supervision=true;kind staysfeedforward. New canonical future RL identity `boosted-outcome-cnn-c32-h128-4abf38ebb1` prevents resuming/overwriting ordinary boosted or prior full/residual RL policies. Old canonical IDs remain unchanged. Same-seed initialization is tensor-identical between ordinary boosted and outcome variant (no extra layer/parameter/RNG draw). Train from scratch;do not initialize this comparison from an already RL-trained actor.

Objective per batch:move cross-entropy +0.5*outcome MSE. Shared encoder and existing linear+tanh value head are trainable;the value loss supplies encoder gradients from the start. Historical own-side final outcome targets win+1/loss−1/draw+.1,**undiscounted**,matching the literal game-outcome prediction task rather than estimating current-policy return. Subsequent PPO usesgamma.99 and different behavior/opponents,so transfer remains an empirical question. Outcome targets require fow-v1,recognized gameplay termination andno bot failure. Invalid/failure outcomes are masked only for value supervision;their existing valid move examples remain,keeping move dataset/split/count matched. No hidden replay board fields are consulted.

`training/outcomes.py` subclasses the existing BoostedReplayDataset and reuses the same compact feature cache,adding locked/atomically built per-position float32targets and validity sidecars underoutcome-v1. Sidecars check positional/game-boundary alignment;counts,target moments and masked games/positions are recorded. Recipe remains50epochs,batch128,seed7980,AdamW betas(.9,.99),eps1e-8,decay.01,globalclip5,startLR1e-4/peak1e-3/floor1e-5,5820warmupupdates then cosine overthe50epochs. Both objectives share that optimizer/schedule;no separate high critic LR is introduced. Select best by the existing8192-position legal-move accuracy probe,not a new outcome-selection rule. Thus the intended treatment is joint outcome supervision with an explicitfixed.5MSE coefficient;this is one seed and cannot establish training-seed robustness. Move-only baseline labels/data are retained.

Existing metrics.loss remains move CE for compatible plots/comparisons;newtotal_loss andoutcome dictionaries distinguish combined objective from policy quality. Outcome metrics:eligible-position MSE/RMSE/MAE/EV,prediction/target means/stds,win/loss sign accuracy(excluding draws),and training-mean constant MSE onvalidation. Existing per-layer/global gradients,update ratios,LR,legal metrics,activation statistics and final histograms continue. Newoutcome_training.png plots joint loss and outcome metrics byepoch. ### Findings, takeaways, and next directions

1. **Joint outcome supervision learned a meaningful historical signal.** Held-out EV is about0.22, decisive-position accuracy is about69%, and MSE is about22%lower than the training-mean constant. The small mean bias at43 shows that this is more than mean calibration. This is a promising PPO initialization, not evidence that fresh on-policy EV will also reach0.22.
2. **The move-prediction cost is small in this run.** The selected joint checkpoint trails move-only best by0.195legal-accuracy points. At matched final50, full raw accuracy is only0.118points lower. No arena benchmark was run, so neither move accuracy nor outcome accuracy establishes stronger play.
3. **Dense concentration and scale improved substantially; clipping and rare spikes did not.** At50, the dominant dense-unit share is52.99%versus96.37%, and dense std is1.244versus21.739. These are useful representation-health observations, but one unit still carries about half of activity and the trunk remains sparse. They do not demonstrate that optimization is fully stabilized.
4. **Wait for the wide run before judging capacity.** Compare completed64/256joint pretraining against this32/128joint run using the same move and outcome metrics, constant baseline, gradient/activation diagnostics and training budget. Its31-epoch download remains a partial snapshot of a running job.
5. **The decisive next test is fresh-game transfer.** Benchmark the joint actor against frozen full2200/residual-best1200, measure its critic against current-policy discounted returns, then compare the same400-update PPO budget with the original boosted protocol. Preserve the trained value head, as the implementation does. Historical undiscounted labels and current discounted returns differ; calibration and adaptation are expected. No PPO or arena was launched by this analysis.
6. **Keep checkpoint selection explicit.** Epoch43 is the established policy-selected candidate. Epoch50 can be evaluated as a separately identified final candidate; it should not silently replace43 because another metric looks better. Multiple training/evaluation seeds and game-level uncertainty would strengthen conclusions. A breakdown by game phase or remaining decisions would test how much outcome accuracy comes from near-terminal positions.

Reproducibility scripts: `work/analyze_boosted_outcome_pretrain.py` and `work/report_boosted_outcome_pretrain.py`. Derived evidence: `out/experiments/boosted-outcome-cnn-28094904/analysis/comparison.json` and `joint-vs-move-only.png`. The JSON contains matched split/recipe checks, three checkpoint SHA256/finite checks, selected/final metrics, per-epoch gradients/update ratios/activation summaries and both training curves. Original checkpoints, metrics and histograms are untouched. These supervised findings belong here; subsequent PPO results belong in RL_EXPERIMENT_HISTORY.md.

### Follow-up decision: retain joint move/outcome pretraining (2026-11-06)

Joint move/outcome pretraining is worth keeping as the working recipe for boosted models, including the pending64/256 wide comparison. The supervised evidence above supports a useful outcome signal with a small move-accuracy tradeoff. Subsequent medium-model PPO results are recorded in RL_EXPERIMENT_HISTORY.md stage60: the100-game frozen-opponent score rose from36% before PPO to59.5% at latest400 and69.5% at selected best320. The prior move-only boosted run scored53.5%/63.5% for latest/best; last50 fresh critic EV/RMSE were0.06802/0.78268 for joint versus0.00497/0.82971 for move-only. This supports retaining the recipe provisionally, not a causal claim that value-head initialization alone helped: joint training also changed encoder/policy, trajectories differ, and only one training seed and100-game benchmarks are available. Critic calibration and large clipped gradients remain unresolved.

The user prefers to keep the existing full latest2200/residual best1200 frozen opponent mixture while the wide boosted model finishes supervised pretraining. A recommended next continuation is400 further medium outcome PPO updates from latest400 to800, preserving the same optimizer state, hyperparameters and exact50/50 opponent balance. Do not introduce boosted checkpoints as opponents or begin PSRO for that comparison. This entry records the recommendation and preference only; no continuation was launched by this documentation change.
